summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of COPD, chronic alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was admitted after being found on a park bench with severe shortness of breath and an oxygen saturation of 85% on room air. A chest X-ray revealed right middle lobe collapse likely due to mucus plugging, and he was treated for COPD exacerbation with prednisone, azithromycin, and bronchodilators. He was also managed for alcohol withdrawal with diazepam, thiamine, and multivitamins. His right olecranon fracture was noted to have worsened with displacement, and orthopedic follow-up was recommended. Hypertension was controlled with amlodipine. Despite clinical improvement, he left the hospital against medical advice before receiving discharge medications or follow-up instructions.
